minutes.headline: Selectmen appointed a patrol officer and set a wiring inspector rate for commercial solar; FY15 budget review began.
minutes.summary: The board heard a member announce he will not seek re-election, appointed a patrol officer, and heard the IT director explain why Mass Broadband prices are too high to adopt. The auditor presented the FY13 audit, described as clean with minor management-letter suggestions. The board set a pay rate for the wiring inspector on commercial solar projects, then began discussing the town manager's preliminary FY15 budget, mainly the street sweeper, road management and town hall needs, and heard committee reports.

attendees.role: presenter, auditor from Powers and Sullivan

votes.motion: Ratify the town manager and chief's appointment of Devon Z O'Brien as patrol officer effective July 20, 2014
Compensate the wiring inspector for commercial solar inspections at the stated hourly rate, one hour minimum, then half-hour increments

budget_items.what_was_said: IT director said current cable broadband per location costs far less than the Mass Broadband vendor quotes, so he does not recommend switching.
Auditor reported a general fund surplus, no free cash needed, revenues over and expenditures under budget, and unassigned fund balance in the range rating agencies like.
Auditor noted a liability with no reserve and a new law allowing a reserve; the town manager said a payout estimate has been budgeted three years running.
New accounting standards will require the unfunded pension liability on the statements; funding schedule runs to 2040.

budget_items.topic: Wiring inspector fee for commercial solar
budget_items.what_was_said: Inspector proposed hourly compensation from the permit fee already collected; the project permit fee was paid already.
Member concerned sweeper not funded and outsourcing cost; DPW director reportedly said a single sweep exceeds a stated amount.
A member noted police, fire and pavement requests and the school not funded at its request, totalling a stated amount, with a balanced budget presented.
A member said the first-pass budget has money available because of a zero percent health insurance increase, and doubted it would repeat.
Warrants for accounts payable were read.

decisions.decision: Police chief amended the appointment to take effect July 20, 2014, keeping the officer as a reserve until the academy.
IT director to continue current cable broadband and revisit Mass Broadband when prices become competitive; he will raise pricing on the conference call.
PACC resignations of two members before the board; the town manager will approve timesheets in the interim.
Board to seek a workshop with the planning board once its warrant articles are substantially done.

what_happened.line: The Select Board voted to ratify the appointment of a patrol officer, with the start date amended to July 20, 2014.
The board voted to pay the wiring inspector an hourly rate, with a one-hour minimum, for commercial solar inspections.
The auditor presented the FY13 audit, reporting a general fund surplus, no free cash needed, and a management letter with minor suggestions.
The board began reviewing the town manager's preliminary FY15 budget, including the street sweeper, roads and town hall needs; a member noted a zero percent health insurance increase.
The IT director recommended staying with current cable broadband and revisiting Mass Broadband when its prices become competitive.

why_it_matters: The FY15 budget discussion shapes what town services and equipment, such as street sweeping and road work, are funded, and so what residents are asked to approve at Town Meeting.
The audit notes a compensated absences liability with no reserve and a pension liability that new accounting standards will require on the statements, both long-term costs paid mostly from taxes.
watch_next: Further Select Board review of the town manager's FY15 budget, including the street sweeper request.
A possible workshop with the planning board once its warrant articles are substantially done.

reconciliation.what: Our minutes against the minutes the town published. caption_error = the same fact the captions rendered badly, resolved by the official reading shown beside the as-heard one; discrepancy = a substantive difference, flagged and not resolved. Neither record is treated as the referee.
reconciliation.summary: The two records agree on both non-procedural votes (the wiring inspector solar fee and the patrol officer appointment), and on the broadband, PACC and planning board workshop decisions in substance. The main difference is that the captions garbled several names and figures, and the official minutes list many items (a roll call, Eagle Scout, thanks letter) that ours omits. Ours has a few figures that the official minutes do not print.
